title: `obj_make_compatible` has cyclomatic complexity 42 and 112 NLOC (thresholds: 15 / 100)
detail: Lizard reports CCN=42 and NLOC=112 for `obj_make_compatible` — the highest complexity in the entire batch. The function contains a deeply nested chain of version-string comparisons that must be read linearly to understand which fields are removed or transformed for each target API version. At CCN=42 there are 42 independent execution paths, making comprehensive testing impractical. Suggested fix: introduce a version-dispatch registry (a `dict` mapping version tuples to transform callables) and apply them in sorted order, reducing each case to a single callable.

title: 5 `setattr(self, 'literal_name', value)` calls; direct attribute assignment is equivalent and clearer
detail: Lines 158, 699, 701, 702 and one more use `setattr(obj, 'constant_string', value)` with a plain string literal. Ruff B010 notes that for known literal names this is no safer than `obj.attr_name = value` and is less readable. Suggested fix: replace each `setattr(obj, 'hw_disk_bus', ...)` with the equivalent direct assignment.
